{{Article header|deck=Core mining identifies fissured asteroids, cracks them with seismic charges, and collects the exposed deposits.}}

'''Core mining''' is the mining method built around finding an asteroid core, placing [[Seismic Charge Launcher|seismic charges]] into fissures, detonating the asteroid safely, and collecting the deposits exposed by the break-up.

{{Draft warning}}

== When to use core mining ==

Core mining is more deliberate than laser mining. The commander searches for a promising asteroid, confirms that it has fissures and valuable contents, places charges, moves clear of the blast, then uses an [[Abrasion Blaster]] and collectors to recover the exposed deposits.

It rewards careful target selection and timing. It also punishes wasted charges, poor positioning, and cargo/refinery neglect, so a new commander should learn the normal collector and refinery loop first.

== Equipment ==

Core mining normally uses:

* [[Pulse Wave Analyser]] — highlights candidate asteroids worth inspecting.
* [[Prospector Limpet Controller]] — confirms contents and deposits before charges are spent.
* [[Seismic Charge Launcher]] — places charges into fissures.
* [[Abrasion Blaster]] — removes exposed deposits after detonation.
* [[Collector Limpet Controller]], [[Refinery]], cargo space, and limpets.
* [[Detailed Surface Scanner]] — useful for finding mapped hotspots before the search begins.

== Workflow summary ==

# Search the ring for promising asteroids with the pulse wave analyser.
# Inspect and prospect candidates rather than firing charges blindly.
# Place seismic charges according to fissure strength and the detonation meter.
# Move to a safe distance before the detonation timer completes.
# Use an abrasion blaster on exposed deposits and collect the released resources.
# Refine, keep or vent commodities according to the run plan.

== Practical notes ==

* A bright pulse-wave return is a clue, not proof of a valuable core.
* The charge meter matters more than simply filling every fissure.
* After detonation, the job is not finished until exposed deposits have been knocked loose and collected.
* Core mining shares equipment with [[Surface Deposit Mining]], but the fissure-and-detonation stage is specific to core asteroids.
